data.title: MBIA Earnings Call Highlights PREPA Progress and Mounting Losses
data.description:
MBIA Inc ((MBI)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

MBIA’s earnings call presented a mixed picture for investors. Management highlighted reduced PREPA exposure, stronger statutory capital, lower leverage, portfolio runoff, and a continued focus on shareholder returns, but those positives were offset by a sharply weaker third-quarter loss, deeply negative book value, declining holding-company liquidity, elevated expenses, and unresolved PREPA litigation.

Quarterly Losses Worsened Despite Better Year-to-Date Results

MBIA reported a consolidated GAAP net loss of $24 million, or $0.49 per share, compared with an $8 million loss, or $0.17 per share, a year earlier. Adjusted net loss was $3 million, or $0.06 per share, versus adjusted net income of $51 million, or $1.03 per share, although management said year-to-date results compared favorably with 2025.

Loss and LAE Benefits Declined Sharply

The company recorded a $12 million loss and loss-adjustment-expense benefit in the quarter, down from $50 million in the prior-year period. The current benefit was mainly driven by higher discount rates lowering reserve values, while National recorded a $4 million expense instead of a $56 million benefit, contributing to a decline in statutory net income to $18 million from $73 million.

National Reduced PREPA Exposure and Improved Capital Metrics

National’s remaining PREPA exposure stood at $390 million of gross par outstanding, plus $35 million of saleable bankruptcy claims, roughly two-thirds below the $1.2 billion outstanding when PREPA entered Title 3 in 2017. Its gross-par-to-statutory-capital leverage ratio improved to 20-to-1 from 24-to-1, while claims-paying resources reached $1.4 billion.

National Capital Increased as Its Portfolio Amortized

National’s statutory capital rose $37 million from year-end 2025 to $974 million, mainly reflecting $39 million of statutory net income during the first nine months. Its insured portfolio continued to perform generally as expected, with gross par outstanding falling about $2.6 billion to approximately $19.7 billion.

MBIA Insurance Corp. Showed Significant Improvement

MBIA Insurance Corp. reported a statutory net loss of $3 million, a major improvement from the $2.025 billion loss in the third quarter of 2025. Lower loss and LAE, which fell to $4 million from $25 million, supported the comparison, while statutory capital rose to $102 million and claims-paying resources increased to $335 million.

Portfolio Runoff Continued at MBIA Insurance Corp.

The insurer’s insured gross par outstanding declined approximately 13% from year-end 2025 to just under $1.8 billion. The reduction was attributed to scheduled amortization, reinforcing the company’s description of MBIA as a runoff operation rather than a growth business.

Book Value Remained Deeply Negative

MBIA’s book value per share fell to negative $46.87 at September 30, down $2.60 from year-end 2025. The decline reflected a $110 million consolidated GAAP loss through the first nine months and larger unrealized investment losses, driven largely by higher interest rates.

Holding-Company Liquidity Declined While Expenses Stayed High

MBIA Inc. had approximately $577 million of corporate-segment assets, including $335 million of unencumbered cash and liquid assets, $124 million pledged to guaranteed investment agreement holders, and $70 million at MBIA Services. Unencumbered liquidity fell from $357 million at year-end, mainly because of debt service and operating expenses, which totaled about $48 million through the first three quarters after $68.25 million in 2025.

Shareholder Returns Remain a Strategic Focus

Since PREPA entered Title 3, MBIA has repurchased more than 80 million shares at an average price of $7.74 and paid an $8-per-share special dividend totaling slightly more than $400 million. Management said total returns to shareholders through buybacks and dividends have exceeded $1 billion, although future decisions must also account for debt and maturities in 2027, 2028, and later years.

National Dividend Expected in December

National is expected to pay MBIA Inc. an as-of-right dividend in December, likely in a similar amount to the past two years and possibly somewhat higher than the $63 million paid last year. Management said National has lacked capacity for share repurchases recently, while its $71 million authorization remains available but would require holding-company liquidity.

PREPA Litigation Continues Without a Clear Resolution

The Title 3 court scheduled oral arguments for November 18, 2026, on summary judgment involving the accounting counterclaim and net-revenue calculation, while the First Circuit is considering an administrative-claim appeal. Management said the oversight board and bondholders remain far apart, although MBIA believes it has a strong case and acknowledged that the outcome is difficult to predict.

PREPA Claims Could Still Be Sold

Management said the co-op agreement does not prevent National from selling its remaining PREPA claims if an attractive price emerges. However, the custodial-receipt market is not deep or liquid, prices can move sharply after court decisions, and the remaining $390 million of insured par is harder to dispose of than claims already sold.

Oversight Board and Legal Changes Could Affect Timing

MBIA said the three vacant oversight-board seats could potentially be filled before the end of 2026, which it believes may help advance the PREPA process. Weil, Gotshal is winding down, but management said MBIA has suitable representation and expects the transition to a new law firm to occur without disruption.

Co-op Agreement Extension Remains Uncertain

The co-op agreement is currently scheduled to remain in effect through August 31, 2027, with no decision yet on a further extension. Management noted that extensions have occurred several times and remain possible, adding another timing variable to the company’s efforts to resolve or monetize its PREPA-related interests.

LCOR Credit Shows Improvement but Still Requires Support

LCOR is making only partial debt-service payments, requiring National to pay the difference through regular claim payments. Management nevertheless pointed to positive developments, including the leasing of another building, and said it believes the credit is moving in a very positive direction.

MBIA Reported No Brightline Exposure

Management stated that MBIA has no direct or indirect exposure to Florida’s Brightline commuter railroad. The clarification addressed an investor question and removed that credit from the list of potential risks affecting the company’s insured portfolio.

Forward-Looking Guidance Centers on Dividends and PREPA Sales

Management expects National to pay its as-of-right dividend in December in an amount similar to recent years, possibly slightly above $63 million, and believes the vacant oversight-board positions could be filled before year-end. MBIA remains in runoff, would seek to sell the company or National as soon as possible, and said PREPA exposure could decline further if attractive prices are available, while the co-op agreement runs through August 2027 with an extension still possible.

Overall, MBIA’s call showed meaningful progress in capital strength, leverage reduction, portfolio runoff, and PREPA exposure reduction, but the investment case remains weighed down by weak quarterly earnings, negative book value, lower liquidity, and high expenses. The timing and value of a broader transaction still depend heavily on PREPA litigation, claims-market conditions, and the pace of regulatory and legal developments.

data.title: Evogene Earnings Call Highlights Pipeline Progress, Financial Strain
data.description:
Evogene Ltd. ((EVGN)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Evogene’s earnings call offered a mixed picture. Management highlighted meaningful progress in its drug-discovery and fungicide programs, but sharply lower revenue, a wider net loss, higher financing costs and continued cash usage weighed on the financial results.

aGVHD Program Enters Candidate-Selection Phase

Evogene selected acute graft-versus-host disease, or aGVHD, for its internal drug-discovery program. Using its ChemPass AI platform, the company generated diverse, patentable small-molecule candidates within months, with nanomolar potency and promising preliminary ADME and toxicology profiles.

Significant Unmet Need in aGVHD

Management said aGVHD affects roughly 30% to 40% of hematopoietic stem-cell transplant recipients. Mortality can reach 50% among patients with steroid-refractory disease, while ruxolitinib remains the only approved second-line treatment.

Experts Support aGVHD Strategy

The program is supported by Dr. Corey Cutler of Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and Professor Dr. Robert Zeiser of University Medical Center of Freiburg. Their guidance covers target selection, disease mechanisms and the clinical development strategy.

AgPlenus Advances Septoria Fungicide Programs

Evogene’s AgPlenus unit advanced two fungicide programs aimed at proteins essential to fungal survival. The targets have not previously been exploited in commercial fungicide development, and TargetSelector and ChemPass AI for Ag are being used to design molecules with novel modes of action.

Fungicide Results Show Strong Activity

Testing showed that the molecules inhibited their intended fungal targets and remained active against Septoria strains resistant to existing fungicides. Some compounds reduced disease severity by 75% on infected plant tissue versus untreated controls, with several findings independently validated by an external research organization.

Potential Beyond Septoria

The molecules also showed activity against other fungal pathogens. Management said the findings could broaden their use across multiple fungal diseases and increase the commercial potential of selected candidates.

Septoria Represents a Large Market

More than 70% of fungicides historically used in European wheat production have targeted Septoria, according to management. The company estimates the related market opportunity at approximately EUR 1.2 billion.

Partner Interest in Novel Fungicides

AgPlenus plans to optimize the molecules and expand biological testing before moving the leading candidates into greenhouse and field evaluations. Early discussions have shown strong potential-partner interest in Septoria solutions based on new modes of action.

aGVHD Candidates Move Toward Testing

Evogene has begun receiving synthesized aGVHD compounds and plans to validate them in Israel and in an adviser’s laboratory. Management said the program remains at an early discovery stage and will require further optimization, characterization and evaluation before IND-enabling work.

Collaborative Programs Continue to Develop

Management said its collaboration programs continue to advance, with new partner results arriving almost monthly. The company expects an updated presentation to show its current pipeline, while a future analyst call will place greater emphasis on collaborations.

Operating Expenses Decline Modestly

For the first nine months of 2026, research and development costs fell to about $4.5 million from $4.6 million, while sales and marketing expenses declined to $0.9 million from $1.1 million. General and administrative expenses edged down to approximately $3.1 million from $3.2 million.

Quarterly Sales Costs Fall

Third-quarter sales and marketing expenses dropped to approximately $0.2 million from $0.4 million a year earlier. The reduction was mainly linked to lower spending at Casterra and AgPlenus.

Nine-Month Revenue Drops Sharply

Revenue for the first nine months of 2026 fell to approximately $0.8 million from $3.2 million in the same period of 2025. Management attributed most of the decline to lower Casterra revenue, as the first half of 2025 included about $2 million in significant seed sales.

Quarterly Revenue Reflects Bayer Agreement End

Third-quarter revenue declined to roughly $0.1 million from $0.3 million in the prior-year quarter. The decrease mainly reflected the conclusion of Evogene’s license and collaboration agreement with Bayer in May 2026.

Quarterly R&D Costs Increase

Third-quarter R&D expenses rose to approximately $1.5 million from $1.1 million. The increase reflected a non-refundable grant recognition of about $0.2 million, a $0.1 million adjustment to government-grant liabilities and U.S. dollar-shekel exchange-rate movements.

Financing Expenses Reverse Prior-Year Benefit

Net financing expenses reached approximately $1.6 million in the first nine months of 2026, compared with net financing income of $0.9 million a year earlier. The change was mainly tied to warrant accounting and revaluation, including $3.8 million of expenses from the February 2026 warrant inducement transaction, partly offset by $2.3 million of income from warrant-liability revaluation.

Discontinued Operations Weigh on Results

Loss from discontinued operations was approximately $0.5 million in the first nine months, compared with income of $4 million in the prior-year period. Third-quarter loss was about $0.06 million, versus income of $7.6 million, with results mainly reflecting Lavie Bio, Biomica and MicroBoost AI for Ag-related expenses.

Net Loss Widens Significantly

Evogene reported a first-nine-month net loss of approximately $10.5 million, up from $2.5 million a year earlier. Third-quarter results swung to a $2.9 million loss from $5.2 million of net income, reflecting lower revenue, higher financing expenses and the absence of prior-year income connected with the ICL transaction.

Cash Balance Remains a Key Focus

As of September 30, 2026, Evogene held approximately $9.2 million in cash, cash equivalents and short-term bank deposits. Consolidated cash usage was about $2.4 million during the third quarter, including a $0.5 million Directors’ and Officers’ insurance payment covering 18 months.

Corporate and Legal Costs Offset Savings

Transaction costs tied to the warrant inducement and additional non-recurring legal expenses related to governance and shareholder matters totaled about $0.4 million for the first nine months and $0.3 million in the third quarter. These costs largely offset lower general and administrative spending across Evogene and its subsidiaries.

Guidance: Preclinical and Field Work Ahead

Evogene said it is working toward IND-enabling studies for its aGVHD program and expects to enter preclinical trials around the middle of next year, when it could begin approaching pharmaceutical companies with early results. For Septoria, the company plans further optimization and testing, followed by greenhouse and field trials for leading compounds, while exploring partnerships over the coming year.

Overall, the call showed a company making notable scientific progress while facing considerable financial pressure. Novel aGVHD and fungicide candidates, external validation and possible partnering interest support the platform, but falling revenue, a wider loss and ongoing cash consumption remain central risks for investors.

The earnings call suggests Evogene is building a potentially valuable pipeline, but its financial recovery depends on translating early research into partnerships, development milestones and commercial revenue. Investors will likely focus on preclinical progress in aGVHD, field data for Septoria and the company’s ability to manage liquidity.

data.title: Youdao Earnings Call: Profitability Advances Despite Revenue Pressure
data.description:
Youdao Inc Adr Class A ((DAO)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Youdao’s earnings call carried a broadly positive tone despite a 12.3% year-over-year revenue decline and weaker sales in Learning Services, Online Marketing Services and Smart Devices. Management emphasized stronger profitability, improving cash generation, expanding AI adoption and confidence that key businesses will return to growth.

Profitability Continues to Improve

Youdao reported third-quarter operating profit of RMB 33.7 million, up 19.2% from a year earlier. The company has now remained operating-profitable for nine consecutive quarters, while its operating margin improved to 2.4% from 1.7%.

Sharp Year-to-Date Cash Flow Recovery

Operating cash flow for the first nine months reached RMB 152.1 million, compared with a RMB 129 million outflow in the same period last year. Management said the company remains on track for rapid full-year operating cash flow growth.

AI Models Gain Early Recognition

Youdao launched Confucius4-R2T2 for real-time speech recognition and Confucius4-T3PO for streaming text translation during the quarter. Both models reached the top position in their respective trending categories on Hugging Face.

AI Subscriptions Lift Learning Services

Learning Services revenue was RMB 609.4 million, while sales of AI-driven subscriptions exceeded RMB 100 million in the third quarter. Subscription sales grew by more than 20% year over year, showing continued demand for AI-enabled learning tools.

Lingshi Retention Remains Strong

Management said Youdao Lingshi’s recent retention rate exceeded 75%. The result was supported by ongoing improvements to its Confucius-powered AI ecosystem and disciplined operating execution.

Personalized Learning Tools Expand

Youdao introduced AI Exam Paper Analysis, which identifies students’ knowledge gaps and recommends what they should study next. AI English essay grading and AI college admission advisers also broadened the company’s personalized learning and decision-support offerings.

Programming Students Post Strong Results

Youdao’s programming students earned four gold, 23 silver and 19 bronze medals at the 43rd National Olympiad in Informatics. The results reinforce the company’s position in advanced programming education.

AI Applications Continue to Gain Users

HiEcho sales more than doubled year over year for the third consecutive quarter. User engagement with AI simultaneous interpretation increased about 30% in the third quarter, while LobsterAI surpassed one million users.

New AI Agents Target Everyday Work

Youdao launched Bage Shuo, a voice agent that transcribes speech and organizes notes, action items, meeting minutes, documents and translations. HiEcho 4 added more agentic features, while LobsterAI 2 enabled users to publish and share interactive dashboards and web pages.

Euler Tutoring Shows High Accuracy

Euler Tutoring uses Confucius to provide interactive mathematics instruction, including visual geometry tools and step-by-step feedback on students’ reasoning. Management said tutoring accuracy reached 95% in testing, with physics prompts planned for a future release.

Online Marketing Margins Expand

Online Marketing Services gross margin rose to 29.6% from 25.4% a year earlier. The improvement of more than 400 basis points marked the second consecutive quarter of year-over-year margin expansion.

Advertising Growth Becomes More Diversified

Advertising revenue from AI applications and short-form dramas each grew more than 50% year over year for the third consecutive quarter. Financial services and automobile advertising also rose by more than 50% in each sector.

YouTube Partnership Supports Global Expansion

Youdao Ads became an inaugural partner in YouTube’s Creator Support program and completed integration with the YouTube Creator Partnerships API. Its YODA AI agent is being tested to support influencer matching, outreach, recruitment and campaign performance management.

Smart Devices Retain Category Leadership

Youdao launched the AI Tutoring Pen 3 and Dictionary Pen A7S Pro. During the November 11 shopping festival, the Dictionary Pen ranked first in category sales on JD.com and Tmall for the seventh consecutive year.

Lower Costs Support Net Income Growth

Total operating expenses fell to RMB 589 million from RMB 659.6 million, with sales and marketing costs declining to RMB 422.2 million. Research and development spending also decreased, while net income attributable to ordinary shareholders rose to RMB 33.4 million from RMB 0.1 million.

Non-GAAP Earnings Improve Materially

Non-GAAP net income increased to RMB 45.9 million from RMB 9.2 million a year earlier. The gain reflected stronger operating profitability alongside tighter control of sales, marketing and research expenses.

Debt Repayment Reduces Interest Costs

Youdao repaid approximately RMB 230 million of intercompany loans to its parent during the first nine months. Management said the repayment significantly reduced interest expense and further strengthened operating cash generation.

Revenue Declines Across Core Segments

Third-quarter net revenue was RMB 1.4 billion, down 12.3% year over year. Total gross profit fell 9.5% to RMB 622.7 million as several businesses faced difficult comparisons and weaker demand.

Learning Services Face Seasonal Timing Pressure

Learning Services revenue declined 5.2% to RMB 609.4 million. Management attributed the decline mainly to a larger share of summer enrollments taking place in the second quarter this year.

Marketing Revenue Reflects a Tough Comparison

Online Marketing Services revenue fell 8.8% to RMB 674.3 million. The company said the decrease was mainly due to a difficult comparison with last year’s third quarter, when more blockbuster games were released.

Smart Device Demand Remains Challenging

Smart Devices revenue dropped 40.9% to RMB 145.2 million, primarily because of weaker demand for smart learning devices. Gross margin also declined to 41.0% from 50.3%, adding pressure to the segment’s contribution.

Quarterly Cash Flow Was Affected by Seasonality

Youdao used RMB 89 million in operating cash during the third quarter. Management attributed the roughly RMB 30 million year-over-year increase in outflow mainly to the seasonal shift in summer course sales and lower course-business gross billings.

Deferred Revenue Moves Lower

Contract liabilities, mainly deferred Learning Services revenue, stood at RMB 771.8 million on September 30, 2026. That was below the RMB 847.7 million recorded at the end of 2025, reflecting changes in the timing and level of course collections.

Management Maintains a Positive Outlook

Youdao expects Learning Services and Online Marketing Services to return to growth in the near future. Management also expects to meet the objectives set at the start of the year for faster improvements in operating profit and operating cash flow, with cash flow remaining stable for the rest of the year.

Full-Year Cash Flow Growth Remains in Focus

The company said strong fourth-quarter course retention should support growth and strengthen cash reserves, while Online Marketing Services is expected to maintain a high revenue base and rapid cash collection. Management also expects the operating improvements to become more visible in 2026, supported by Learning Services cash flow growth and Lingshi retention above 75%.

Youdao’s call balanced near-term revenue pressure against clear progress in profitability, cash generation and AI adoption. Investors will likely focus on whether the company’s expanding AI portfolio, stronger margins and retention gains can drive the promised return to growth.

data.title: ATRenew Earnings Call Highlights Strong Growth and Expansion
data.description:
ATRenew Inc. Sponsored ADR ((RERE)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

ATRenew’s third-quarter earnings call carried a strongly positive tone, with management highlighting faster revenue and operating profit growth, better margins, expanding retail operations, overseas gains, and ample liquidity. Seasonal softness, weaker new-device shipments, higher inventory, rising costs, and slower overseas activity were acknowledged, but expense ratios improved and growth expectations remained firm.

Revenue and Operating Profit Accelerate

ATRenew reported third-quarter revenue of RMB6.45 billion, up 25.3% from a year earlier and above the high end of its guidance. Non-GAAP operating profit rose 50.7% to more than RMB210 million, while the operating margin expanded 55 basis points to 3.3%.

Product and Service Revenue Both Increase

Net product revenue grew 27.0% to RMB6 billion, supported mainly by online sales of pre-owned consumer electronics. Net service revenue increased 6.1% to RMB400 million, driven by the PJT Marketplace and multi-category recycling services.

Higher Margins and a Stronger Retail Mix

The 1P business gross margin improved to 14.4% from 13.4% a year earlier. Management credited high-efficiency C2B recycling, compliant refurbishment capabilities, and a broader retail mix, with 1P2C revenue rising to 41.4% of product revenue from 36.4%.

1P and Retail Expansion Continue

ATRenew continued to prioritize its self-operated 1P business, with 1P2C retail revenue increasing 44.3% year over year. Its share of product revenue rose by five percentage points, showing that retail is becoming a larger part of the company’s business.

Store and Door-to-Door Network Expands

As of September 30, ATRenew operated 2,130 stores in 303 cities, nine more than at the end of June. Its door-to-door service team exceeded 2,600 employees at quarter-end and reached more than 2,800 by the end of October, supporting long-term goals of 5,000 stores and 5,000 service members.

More Flexible Fulfillment Capacity

The company shifted its door-to-door staffing model toward a larger share of flexible capacity that can be trained and deployed quickly. Management said the change improved fulfillment flexibility while helping optimize related expenses.

Refurbishment Revenue Posts Strong Growth

Revenue from refurbished products increased 34.6% year over year, reflecting the growing role of compliant refurbishment. On-demand refurbishment represented more than 40% of that business and created virtual inventory for sale without adding pressure from unsold refurbished goods.

PJT Adds AI Tools for Merchants

PJT integrated AI models and intelligent trading tools to help sellers develop more effective pricing strategies. Its 3P warehousing inspection penetration reached 85.3%, up about 6.7 percentage points year over year, while new tools supported buyer sourcing and the Like-new device marketplace.

PJT Merchant Base Reaches 2.52 Million

The marketplace continued building its specialty buyer model and expanding into fragmented and lower-tier markets. Registered PJT merchants totaled 2.52 million at the end of September, giving the platform a broader base for future transaction growth.

Paipai Shows Platform Improvement

Paipai required fewer subsidies to support merchant activity, while B2C platform service revenue rose significantly from the previous quarter. The platform is focusing on attracting more small and medium-sized merchants, improving transaction experiences, and strengthening price competitiveness.

Multi-Category Recycling Gains Momentum

Revenue from multi-category recycling services grew 38% year over year in the third quarter, and the company operated 971 stores. A designer-toys-themed store opened in September after a racquet-sports location launched in May, with both stores performing better than management expected.

Themed Store Pilot Program Expands

ATRenew plans to continue small-scale themed-store pilots in Shanghai and test categories such as billiards cues, ski equipment, camera gear, and bags and luggage. Management expects the network to reach 10 themed stores by the end of 2026.

International Revenue Surges

Overseas product revenue reached RMB240 million in the quarter, up 150% year over year and equal to 4% of 1P product revenue. ATRenew continued building sales channels in Dubai, where its office began trial operations in October, and expects overseas revenue to reach RMB1 billion for the full year.

Expense Ratios Improve Despite Higher Spending

Absolute operating expenses increased, but several expense ratios moved in the right direction. Non-GAAP fulfillment costs fell to 7.9% of revenue from 8.4%, selling and marketing costs declined to 6.9% from 7.0%, and research and development costs dropped to 1.0% from 1.2%, while general and administrative costs held at 1.3%.

Liquidity Supports Investment and Buybacks

Cash, restricted cash, short-term investments, and funds receivable from payment providers totaled RMB1.94 billion at September 30, 2026. The company repurchased about 1.6 million ADS for roughly US$6.6 million during the quarter and had approximately US$28.6 million remaining under its current buyback authorization.

Hong Kong Listing Application Submitted

ATRenew confidentially submitted an application for a Main Board listing on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. Management said a listing could improve access to Hong Kong’s capital markets and broaden the investor base, although approval remains subject to the required filing and review process.

Long-Term Capability Building Remains a Priority

Management said it will continue investing in the self-operated 1P business and develop the AHS Recycle brand from a recycling service into a retail platform. Other priorities include fulfillment, supply chain, overseas B2B operations, compliant exports, recycling platforms, and automation technology.

Seasonal Third-Quarter Softness

Management described the third quarter as a traditionally slower period for the pre-owned electronics industry. Recycling volumes tend to be lower than in the second and fourth quarters as flagship devices begin launching late in the period, while limited consumer promotions can weigh on retail activity.

New-Device Shipments Decline Across the Industry

Rapidly rising memory prices contributed to higher prices for new smartphones, laptops, tablets, and other electronics. Management also cited changes in product launch timing and said overall new-device shipments declined year over year, creating a more difficult industry backdrop.

Inventory Rises as the Business Expands

Inventory stood at RMB1.31 billion at the end of September, down about RMB80 million from June but up approximately RMB240 million from the end of 2025. The increase reflected wider self-operated recycling and trading activity, higher pre-owned device prices, and the slower turnover typical of growing 1P2C retail operations.

Overseas Revenue Eases Sequentially

Third-quarter overseas revenue was slightly below the seasonally strong second quarter. Management attributed the decline to slower China-sourced supply and softer overseas B2B trading activity, even as international revenue remained well ahead of the prior year.

Operating Costs Rise in Absolute Terms

Non-GAAP fulfillment expenses increased 17.2% to RMB510 million, while selling and marketing expenses rose 23.6% to RMB450 million. General and administrative expenses grew 27.0% to RMB94 million and research and development expenses increased 10.0% to RMB72 million, mainly because of higher personnel costs.

Management Reviews the 2027 Operating Environment

ATRenew is preparing its 2027 budget while watching macroeconomic conditions, consumer trends, and the effect of lower new-device shipments on recycling supply. Store openings and door-to-door expansion will be adjusted according to city tiers and seasonal demand.

Revenue Growth Guidance Remains Strong

For the fourth quarter, ATRenew expects revenue of RMB7.78 billion to RMB7.88 billion, representing year-over-year growth of 24.4% to 26.0%. Full-year 2026 revenue is expected to reach RMB27.03 billion to RMB27.11 billion, up 28.3% to 28.8%, while overseas revenue is projected at RMB1 billion.

Long-Term Targets Stay in Place

The company maintained its long-term goals of 5,000 stores and a 5,000-member door-to-door service team nationwide. It also expects to have 10 themed stores by the end of 2026 and said it is preparing for healthy long-term growth and greater trading penetration in 2027.

ATRenew’s call combined strong quarterly execution with clear investment in retail, refurbishment, logistics, technology, and international operations. While seasonal demand, industry shipment declines, inventory growth, and higher costs remain risks, improving margins, strong liquidity, rapid revenue growth, and stable guidance gave the quarter an encouraging profile for investors.
